newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile police break up march with water, tear gas.
newsitem.headline: Chile police break up march with water, tear gas.

text.p: Police using water cannons and tear gas broke up a street march by striking civil servants in downtown Santiago on Wednesday, a few days before nationwide municipal elections.
The truck-mounted water cannons, a familiar sight in Chile during General Augusto Pinochet's former military regime, drenched and dispersed the marchers.
The workers were heading for a rally outside the headquarters of Chile's main labour confederation, the CUT, when police moved in with water and tear gas.
Fourteen civil servants' unions called the one-day strike to demand wage increases and to protest against plans to privatise some state services, which strikers say will mean thousands of layoffs.
Municipal workers have been on strike for more than a week, causing garbage to pile up on streets in some cities. Teachers last week ended a two-week walkout that shut the country's public schools.

Bus drivers, public health clinic workers and copper miners have also staged strikes over the past few months, all demanding wage increases in line with, or higher than, Chile's economic growth of about seven percent a year.

Government officials accused labour leaders of trying to whip up conflicts to create a feeling of insecurity before the municipal elections on Sunday and pressure the government into making inflationary wage increases.
"What's clear is that with these strikes, certain people are trying to create a climate of confusion before the elections...but they won't succeed," Interior Minister Carlos Figueroa said.
President Eduardo Frei's Christian Democratic party is tipped in most opinion polls to win a plurality of mayoral seats in the elections.
